text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- The former deputy head of police intelligence is arrested on a military court order for illegally obtaining documents related to state security.
- The Turkish army chief authorises military legal action against ex-prime minister Tansu Ciller over allegations she worked for a foreign intelligence service.
MILLIYET
- The Committee to Protect Journalists gives jailed newspaper editor Isk Yurtcu an award at his prison in the western Turkish town of Saray.
- The new anti-Islamist government's price rises continue at full swing. On top of a rise in petroleum product prices, it increases motorway and telecommunication fees.
HURRIYET
- The new under-secretary at the Treasury says he will not bow to any political pressure.
- Ray Sigorta, a company in the Dogan Group, is to be floated on the Istanbul stock exchange.
YENI YUZYIL
- A state security prosecutor examines the purchase by the Ciller family of a farm in the western resort of Kusadasi which was allegedly the scene of illegal activities.
- The new government seeks to liberalise suitcase trading, worth an estimated $12-13 billion annually, with measures aimed at both registering the trade and expanding it.
RADIKAL
- Foreign Minister Ismail Cem says Turkey's prime target is to become a full member of the European Union despite a recent EU report excluding Turkey from expansion plans.
CUMHURIYET
- Deputy Prime Minister Bulent Ecevit will go to northern Cyprus with a delegation of eight ministers on Sunday to celebrate the twenty-third anniversary of the Turkish invasion.
DUNYA
- An EU report says Turkey should move towards renewable resources to produce energy.
ZAMAN
- The Islamic world celebrated the anniversary of the Prophet Mohammad's birth on Wednesday night.
